quote: A meta-analysis of 10 studies was performed to determine the impact of the PCSK9 R46L variant on CAVS, and the authors found that CAVS was less prevalent in carriers of this variant (odds ratio: 0.80 [95% confidence interval: 0.70 to 0.91]; p = 0.0011) compared with noncarriers.
summary: The PCSK9 loss-of-function R46L variant lowers calcific aortic valve stenosis risk, and PCSK9 antibody reduced calcification in valve cells; no UC data.

quote: A crucial issue in the evaluation of the benefit of the anti-inflammatory activity is the frequent discordance between a beneficial activity on a major risk factor and associated changes of hsCRP, as in the case of statins vs PCSK9 antagonists.
summary: Cardiovascular review noting PCSK9 antagonists lower lipids without matching changes in hsCRP; no UC data.

quote: The apolipoprotein B autoantibody and anti-PCSK9 antibody reduced the level of LDL and plaques in animal studies, but failed to significantly reduce carotid inflammation plaques in clinical trials.
summary: Review of antibody therapies for atherosclerosis; anti-PCSK9 antibodies lower LDL but did not clearly reduce plaque inflammation in trials.

quote: Thus, the aim of this narrative review was to evaluate the anti-inflammatory properties of currently available lipid-lowering medications including statins, ezetimibe, bile acid sequestrants (BAS), proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitors, fibrates, omega-3 fatty acids, and niacin, as well as dietary supplements and novel drugs used in modern times.
summary: Narrative review of anti-inflammatory effects of lipid-lowering drugs including PCSK9 inhibitors; no UC data.

quote: PCSK9 inhibitor significantly reduced the risk of SLE but increased the risk of asthma and CD.
summary: Drug-target Mendelian randomization of PCSK9 across autoimmune diseases found effects on SLE, asthma and Crohn's disease; UC was tested but no effect was reported.

quote: QA altered serum galactose metabolism, promoted SREBP-2 and LDLR, inhibited IDOL, FMO3 and PCSK9 expression in liver of HFD-induced Apoe-/- mice.
summary: Quinic acid lowered liver Pcsk9 expression among several lipid genes in atherosclerotic mice; not related to colitis.

quote: There are several therapeutic strategies including Proprotein Convertase Subtilisin/Kexin 9 (PCSK9) inhibitors, inclisiran, bempedoic acid, Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), and nutraceuticals that promise improvement in the atheromatous plaque from a molecular point of view, because have actions on the exposure of the LDL-Receptor (LDL-R), on endothelial dysfunction, activation of macrophages, on lipid oxidation, formations on foam cells, and deposition extracellular lipids.
summary: Atherosclerosis therapy review listing PCSK9 inhibitors among lipid-lowering strategies; no UC data.

quote: It has been shown that CRISPR-Cas9 can be applied to knock out proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) or block PCSK9, resulting in lowering low-density lipoprotein cholesterol.
summary: Review of CRISPR-Cas9 in autoimmune disease that mentions PCSK9 knockout only as an example of lowering LDL cholesterol.
AAV-PCSK9 is used only as a tool to induce hypercholesterolemia in a TRPM2 atherosclerosis study; the paper is not about PCSK9.

quote: Genetically proxied inhibition of PCSK9 increased the risk of IBD, UC and CD, while inhibition of CETP decreased the risk of CD.
summary: Drug-target Mendelian randomization found that genetically proxied PCSK9 inhibition raised the risk of ulcerative colitis (OR about 2.1), suggesting inhibition may harm.

quote: Out of the 341 drug targets identified through their association with blood lipids (HDL-C, LDL-C and triglycerides), we robustly prioritize 30 targets that might elicit beneficial effects in the prevention or treatment of CHD, including NPC1L1 and PCSK9, the targets of drugs used in CHD prevention.
summary: Drug-target Mendelian randomization prioritizes PCSK9 as a causal lipid target for coronary heart disease; no UC data.

quote: Furthermore, some biomarkers showed poor correlations between plasma and serum, including PCSK9, an important regulator of cholesterol homeostasis.
summary: PCSK9 is one of several markers with poor plasma versus serum correlation in an obesity biomarker comparison; no UC data.

quote: Interestingly, miR-26 better reduced intima-media thickness (IMT) than PCSK9 or CT-1 knockout.
summary: Review of miR-26 in atherosclerosis that only compares it with PCSK9 knockout and lists PCSK9 inhibitors in trials.

quote: Hence, inhibition of PCSK9 has become a very potent tool for the treatment of hypercholesterolemia.
summary: Review of PCSK9 roles in chronic liver disease, including inflammation and lipid metabolism; no UC data.

quote: Several proteins were found to mediate the associations between some modifiable factors and CAD, with PCSK9, C1S, AGER (advanced glycosylation end product-specific receptor), and MST1 (mammalian Ste20-like kinase 1) exhibiting highest frequency among the mediating networks.
summary: Proteome-wide Mendelian randomization lists PCSK9 among proteins mediating obesity and lifestyle effects on coronary artery disease; no UC data.

quote: In conclusion, PCSK9 inhibition attenuated TNBS-induced rat colitis through anti-inflammatory effect under inactivation of TLR4/NF-κB, suggesting potential therapeutic strategy in IBD.
summary: PCSK9 is raised in TNBS colitis in rats, and adenoviral PCSK9 inhibition reduced weight loss, MPO activity, colonic damage and inflammatory cytokines via TLR4/NF-κB.

quote: Nonetheless, a group of genes was differentially regulated in the EpOCs and d-EpOCs of patients with UC, including genes associated with antimicrobial defence (ie, LYZ, PLA2G2A), with secretory (ie, ZG16, CLCA1) and absorptive (ie, AQP8, MUC12) functions, and with a gastric phenotype (ie, ANXA10, CLDN18 and LYZ).
summary: PLA2G2A is one of many genes differentially regulated in organoids derived from UC patients; no gene-specific result is given.

quote: Using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), we measured the mRNA expression levels of key Paneth cell antimicrobial peptides (DEFA5, DEFA6, LYZ, PLA2G2A), inflammatory cytokines [interkelukin 6 (IL6) and IL8], and a marker of epithelial cell content, villin (VIL1) in 106 samples from both affected ileum (inflamed Crohn's disease cases, n = 44) and unaffected ileum (non-inflamed; Crohn's disease cases, n = 51 and controls, n = 11).
summary: PLA2G2A mRNA was measured in ileal Crohn's disease alongside other Paneth cell peptides, but the reported findings concern alpha-defensins.

quote: Finally, we show that these functions of activated Notch1 are present in the mucosa of ulcerative colitis, mediating cell proliferation, goblet cell depletion, and ectopic expression of PLA2G2A, thereby contributing to the regeneration of the damaged epithelia.
summary: PLA2G2A is a Notch1 downstream gene and is ectopically expressed in ulcerative colitis mucosa, where Notch activation supports epithelial regeneration.

quote: In addition to host defense molecules such as α-defensins, lysozyme, and Pla2g2a, Paneth cells also produce and release proinflammatory mediators as components of secretory granules.
summary: Review of Paneth cell alpha-defensins that names Pla2g2a only as one Paneth cell host defense molecule.

quote: Proinflammatory genes Cxcl1, Ccl2, Il1b, Lcn2, Pla2g2a, Saa3, S100a9, Nos2, Reg2, and Reg3g, and profibrogenic extracellular matrix genes Col1a1, Col1a2, Col3a1, and Lum (lumican), encoding a collagen-associated proteoglycan, were up-regulated at the active/chronic inflammatory stages.
summary: Pla2g2a is one of many proinflammatory genes up-regulated in chronic TNBS colitis in mice, with no gene-specific analysis.

quote: In normal colon, PLA2G2A and PLA2G12A were expressed at high levels, PLA2G2D, PLA2G5, PLA2G10 and PLA2G12B at moderate levels, and PLA2G1B, PLA2G2F and PLA2G3 at low levels.
summary: PLA2G2A is highly expressed in normal human colon; its expression was not highlighted as altered in colorectal adenocarcinoma, where PLA2G3 was the marker.

quote: C. rodentium infection induced expression of several antimicrobial peptides such as RegIIIγ and Pla2g2a in the intestine which was critically dependent on Stat3 activation.
summary: Pla2g2a induction in the intestine during Citrobacter infection depends on epithelial Stat3, which protects barrier function; Pla2g2a itself was not perturbed.

quote: Three major candidate genes (Cd14, Gbp1, Pla2g2a) showed prominent expression differences between B6- and C3-Il10(-/-) as well as between B6 and C3 wild-type mice, which was confirmed by semiquantitative or real-time RT-PCR.
summary: Pla2g2a expression differs between colitis-susceptible and resistant mouse strains within QTL intervals, making it a candidate gene; follow-up focused on Cd14.

quote: Under IL-6 trans-signaling conditions 36 genes were upregulated, including PLA2G2A, IL13RA1, MUC1, and SOD2.
summary: PLA2G2A is one of 36 genes induced by IL-6 trans-signaling in airway smooth muscle cells; not about the gut.
